content.text: : cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Replacement therapy: adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) and congenital adrenal hyperplasia (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synthesis)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): diagnosis of Cushing’s syndrome
•Treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases:  RA, ulcerative colitis, asthma, SLE, eye and skin inflammation
•Treatment of allergic reactions: drug, serum, and transfusion reactions
•Immunosuppression: prevention of graft rejection after transplantation
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
Indications: used mainly for anti-inflammatory effects as first line agents for relief of sxs in chronic inflammatory disease states
•RA, acute gouty arthritis, acute ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis

: GI (irritation, gastritis, PUD, bleeding), increased bleeding time, decreased GFR, ischemia, acute renal failure, salt/water retention, CHF risk, rash, SJS, asthmatics (bronchospasm, dyspnea, wheezing), aseptic meningitis, exacerbation of anemia, rebound HA
: irreversible inhibition of both COX1 & COX2

: GI irritation, erosive gastritis, increased bleeding time, gastric ulceration/bleeding, salicylism (tinnitus, deafness, HA, confusion, increased pulse & respiratory rates), hyperventilation, respiratory alkalosis, hypersensitivity (rash, SJS/TEN), Reyes syndrome (fulminating hepatitis w/ cerebral edema)
: GI bleeding/ulcerations, CNS (HA, vertigo, confusion), blood dyscrasias (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia)
: serious GI toxicity, edema, HA, dizziness, rash, severe skin reactions
: osteoarthritis, RA, juvenile RA, acute pain, primary dysmenorrhea, ankylosing spondylitis
: pts w/ aspirin triad; sulfa allergy
•use w/ great caution or not at all in pts w/ chronic renal failure, severe heart disease, & hepatic failure
•reserve use for pts at highest risk of NSAID-induced gastropathy
•nephrotoxicity, greater prothrombotic effect, reduced incidence of GI bleeding/ulcers
